items.title: Under weak association and locally finite components the sheaf of meromorphic functions is the product of the skyscrapers at the generic points
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a scheme whose weakly associated points are generic points of components and whose components are locally finite, the sheaf of meromorphic functions is simultaneously the direct sum and the product of the skyscrapers at the generic points, with consequences for meromorphic sections of quasi-coherent modules, the description of nonzerodivisors, the total quotient rings of local rings and of affine coordinate rings, and the identification of rational with meromorphic functions (statement lines 6034-6073). The counted proof has two layers: it reduces everything to the identity for the sheaf of meromorphic functions, rewritten as a pushforward along the coproduct morphism from the local rings at the generic points, and it verifies that identity on affine opens using the product decomposition of the total ring of fractions, from which quasi-coherence, the nonzerodivisor statement and the stalk statement follow (proof lines 6075-6132). It is H2: the reductions and the affine computation are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the total ring of fractions and pullback statements.
